reconcile.note: Clarke explains that Solomon appears last among Bathsheba's four sons because the genealogy is arranged to continue through him, not by birth order.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Was Solomon David's second or fourth son by Bathsheba?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/solomon.html) (2013).

sides.snippet: Nathan departed to his house. Yahweh struck the child that Uriah's wife bore to David, and it was very sick.
sides.verseText: Nathan departed to his house. Yahweh struck the child that Uriah's wife bore to David, and it was very sick.

sides.snippet: and these were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon, four, of Bathshua the daughter of Ammiel;
